journal_lines: §oSmelled iron and salt together. Low tide had pulled back from the rock shelf. Two different kinds of work waiting.
§aFish in the pools, §lcopper§a in the wet stone above the waterline. Hunter and miner split the shore between them.
Crabs went to the hunter. The exposed seam went to the miner. Efficient division.
§aThe tide does the sorting — everything worth taking ends up at the margin. Came home with both bags heavy.
Rock shelf only visible at low water. Timed it right. Hunter worked the pools, miner worked the cliff face.
§oSeaweed and old iron — two strong smells. Both came home with us.
§aThe water had left ore deposits in the cracks of the rock. §lTide pool§a work rewards the patient nose.
Worked until the water came back. The water gave fair warning. Came home before the pools filled again.
